titulo: One Collar Press Makes a Plain Shirt Look Tailored

A good roll is a soft curve. A poor one is a hard crease, or no curve at all.

The stand was not always part of the shirt. In my grandmother's time, collars were often detachable, held on with a small button at the back and two at the front. Here is a check for the days when you wear a jacket. Put the jacket on over the shirt and stand in front of the mirror. This cloth is your pressing cloth, and it matters more than the iron.

About those collar stays. Some are metal, cool and slightly heavy; some are thin plastic, and some are nothing more than a folded piece of cardboard. I have seen a man use the cardboard from a box of matches. If the stays are bent, replace them; a bent stay makes a bent collar, and no iron can straighten a collar around a crook

The fabric does not remember the iron. It remembers the shape it cools in.

If you do not own a pressing board, you do not need one. A thick towel folded twice on a table will do, and a rolled magazine under the collar gives you the curve.
